about: What the house takes from a pot (scope-v1 module 4, design prompt flows 4 and 5). Rake is the table type's rate of the pot (5%), no more than the table type's cap, rounded down to whole ₹50 chips. While the bad-beat jackpot is live, ₹100 more is dropped into it from every pot above ₹5,000 (not from a pot of exactly ₹5,000). The pull is the rake and the drop together: the chips the dealer takes from the pot. Nothing ever rounds up. The cap is applied when the rate's share of the pot is more than the cap; a share exactly at the cap is not capped. Every case here is a ₹6,000-cap table.

cases.description: Design prompt flow 4: a ₹48,000 pot with the jackpot live. Rake ₹2,400, drop ₹100, pull ₹2,500.
Design prompt flow 5, at the cap: 5% of a ₹1,40,000 pot is ₹7,000, so the rake is the ₹6,000 cap.
Exactly at the cap: 5% of ₹1,20,000 is ₹6,000. The cap changes nothing, so it is not applied.
Just over the cap: 5% of ₹1,20,050 is ₹6,002.50, more than the cap, so the rake is the ₹6,000 cap.
Just under the cap: 5% of ₹1,19,000 is ₹5,950, a whole number of chips.
₹50 boundary: 5% of ₹48,990 is ₹2,449.50, which rounds down to ₹2,400.
₹50 boundary on a small pot: 5% of ₹4,950 is ₹247.50, which rounds down to ₹200; no drop at or under ₹5,000.
A pot of exactly ₹5,000 is not above ₹5,000: rake ₹250 and no drop.
The first pot above ₹5,000: ₹5,050 gives 5% of ₹252.50, so rake ₹250, and the ₹100 drop.
A pot too small for a chip of rake: 5% of ₹950 is ₹47.50, which rounds down to ₹0.
Zero: an empty pot takes nothing.
Before the bad-beat jackpot is live there is no drop: a ₹48,000 pot gives rake ₹2,400 and pull ₹2,400.
